[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
John Glasgow was born about 1794 (exact birthplace not yet proven). He worked as a farmer and was recorded in '''Drumgreenagh''' townland, Derrynoose parish, County Armagh, in 1839.<ref name="Freeholders1839">"Ireland, Ulster Freeholders," entry for '''John Glasgow''', farmer, Drumgreenagh, Armagh, 1839; reference T/808/14961, vol. 123, p. 1, line 151.</ref>

A holding at Drumgreenagh/Killyreavy associated with the Glasgow name appears again in the land valuation compiled 1 Dec 1864 (after John’s death), with landlord '''William Kirk'''.<ref name="Griffiths1864">''Ireland, Griffith’s Valuation, 1847–1864'', Derrynoose parish (Killyreavy/Drumgreenagh), entry dated 1 Dec 1864; occupier recorded as Glasgow; landlord William Kirk.</ref>

Known children—identified from Irish civil marriage records that name their father as '''John Glasgow'''—include:
* '''Mary Jane Glasgow''', married '''Samuel Boyd''' on 15 Jun 1854 at Derrynoose, County Armagh.<ref name="Mary1854">"Ireland, Civil Registration, 1845–1913," marriage of '''Samuel Boyd''' & '''Mary Jane Glasgow''', 15 Jun 1854, Derrynoose, Armagh; FamilySearch ARK: https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QGV8-X359</ref><ref>"Ireland, Marriages, 1619–1898," index entry naming father '''John Glasgow'''; FamilySearch ARK: https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FGXJ-4YD</ref>
* '''Sarah Anne Glasgow''', married '''James Sloan''' on 5 Dec 1862 (record names her father as '''John Glasgow''').<ref name="Sarah1862">"Ireland, Civil Registration, 1845–1913," marriage of '''James Sloan''' & '''Sarah Anne Glasgow''', 5 Dec 1862; FamilySearch ARK: https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QGV8-J5BV</ref>
* '''Elizabeth Glasgow''', married '''Thomas Lennon''' on 15 Jan 1868 (indexed also as '''Glasson''' and '''Leemon''').<ref name="Elizabeth1868">"Ireland, Marriages, 1619–1898," marriage of '''Thomas Lennon''' & '''Elizabeth Glasgow''', 15 Jan 1868; FamilySearch ARK: https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FGZ6-YGT</ref><ref>"Ireland, Civil Registration, 1845–1913," variant index ('''Elizabeth Glasson''' to '''Thomas Leemon'''), 15 Jan 1868; FamilySearch ARK: https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QGY7-Z684</ref>

John is reported to have died on '''30 Apr 1849''' (citation still needed).
A marriage for Elizabeth Glasgow and Leemon was registered on 15 January 1868 in the Armagh district.<ref>[https://geni.nidirect.gov.uk/search/marriage GRONI civil marriage index], 15 January 1868, Armagh district, M/1868/Q1/86/2/26.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Drumgreenagh father hypothesis ===

The older Drumgreenagh farmer John [[Glasgow-4031]] is the preferred probable father of the later farmer John [[Glasgow-3439]], at 64% subjective confidence. The combined argument is the same full name, the same specific townland and farming occupation, and a normal two-generation chronology. The older John was already a married farmer in 1786; the younger account’s approximate 1794 birth fits a child of that household. It is a more specific family comparison than a generic same-surname Armagh or Scottish father. Prefer this direct local lineal model over leaving the later four-child household disconnected from its already identified earlier surname household. The connection is an inference from the combined evidence, not a parent clause or an implication of the connectivity score.

No source names the younger John’s father. The older man’s purchased property was at Lislea, although he resided at Drumgreenagh; no inspected title chain proves that he and the 1839 farmer occupied the same farm. The 1828 Drumgreenagh John probate-index entry is not treated as a proved death, inheritance or link between them: its document type, individual identity and surviving text remain unresolved. Nathaniel-4014 is another older local relative and possible father; an uncle, other collateral, another John, or another unrepresented father remains possible. Both 1786 adults lack recorded ages. The younger John’s 1794 birth is uncertain and has no recovered primary age source in this review, so it cannot absolutely exclude his being the 1786 man at an older age. The preferred father model keeps the two accounts separate without claiming that distinction proved or merging them. Jane Murphy is the older John’s documented wife, but is not assigned as the younger John’s mother. All vital fields, spouses, children and earlier parent grades remain unchanged. The 64% is an individual comparative judgment for this entire father-profile proposition, including the profile and generation assumptions, not a measured probability.

Verify the 1839 freeholder entry and the source of the reported 1794 birth/1849 death. Identify the type of the 1828 probate entry. Trace the Drumgreenagh and Lislea leases, rent rolls and valuation holdings for an explicit son or successor, and test Nathaniel as a separate family option.<ref name="DrumgreenaghFamily2026">[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJW-VDTD Registry of Deeds, John Glasgow and Jane Murphy; deed 13 February 1786, registered 22 December 1792; previously inspected account reused]; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/search/results?datasetname=ireland%2C%20ulster%20freeholders&firstname=john&lastname=glasgow Ireland, Ulster Freeholders: John Glasgow, farmer, Drumgreenagh, 1839; PRONI T/808/14961 vol.123 p.1 line151; held citation, original not rechecked]. Existing source accounts reconsidered 20 October 2026; original entries not newly inspected.</ref>


* '''Residence & Land''' — The 1839 freeholder entry for a farmer '''John Glasgow''' in Drumgreenagh aligns with later valuation evidence in Killyreavy/Drumgreenagh, Derrynoose parish, where the landlord was '''William Kirk'''. The 1864 valuation date is post-mortem for John and likely reflects continuity of the family holding rather than John himself.<ref name="Freeholders1839" /><ref name="Griffiths1864" />
* '''Children''' — Mary Jane (1854), Sarah Anne (1862), and Elizabeth (1868) are securely linked as his children via marriage records that explicitly name their father as '''John Glasgow'''. Additional Glasgow marriages in the area (e.g., a '''Samuel Glasgow''' indexed 23 Mar 1870) may indicate further children; evidence not yet evaluated.
* '''Name & Place Variants''' — Surname appears as '''Glasgow''' and occasionally '''Glasson''' in indexes; bridegroom Lennon is indexed as '''Lennon/Leemon'''. Townland appears as '''Drumgreenagh/Drumgreeney''' within the civil parish of '''Derrynoose''' (sometimes written '''Killyreavy''').
* '''To Do''' — Seek Church of Ireland or Presbyterian registers for Derrynoose/Keady area for baptisms and burial; consult PRONI Freeholders books, Tithe Applotment (1820s–1830s), and Valuation Revision Books for chain of occupancy; locate primary source for the stated death date (30 Apr 1849).

=== Earlier Drumgreenagh namesake ===
A deed made on 13 February 1786 identifies [[Glasgow-4031|an older John Glasgow]] as a farmer at Drumgreenagh and husband of Jane Murphy. He cannot be this profile, who was born about 1794. The shared residence makes an older-family relationship plausible, but the deed names no child and does not prove that the older John was this John's father.<ref>Registry of Deeds, Ireland, memorial of deed of assignment, David Murphy to John Glasgow, deed dated 13 February 1786, registered 22 December 1792; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJW-VDTD FamilySearch image].</ref>

An 1828 probate-index entry also names John Glasgow of Drumgreenagh, County Armagh. This profile was later documented in the same townland, but his 1849 death prevents treating an 1828 administration as his death without inspecting the record type. The entry may concern the older namesake, but that identity is not yet proved.<ref>[https://apps.proni.gov.uk/ProniNames_IE/SearchPage.aspx PRONI Names, Pre-1858 Wills and Admons search], John Glasgow, Drumgreenagh, 1828.</ref>
